title: Super Micro Shares Surge After Preliminary Results Show Record Backlog and Doubled Margins
excerpt: The AI server maker posted more than $60 billion in new orders during its fiscal fourth quarter and expects gross margins nearly double its earlier forecast, sending shares up 17% after hours.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Super Micro expects gross margins of 15%-17%, doubling prior guidance of 8.2%-8.4%.
  • The company secured over $60 billion in new orders, creating a record backlog.
  • Revenue is projected at the low end of $11 billion to $12.5 billion guidance.
  • Shares surged 17% in after-hours trading, while rivals Dell and HPE also gained.
  • Super Micro's strong results signal ongoing demand for AI infrastructure investments.

Super Micro Computer preliminary results
  • Super Micro Computer expects fiscal Q4 gross margins of 15%–17%, roughly double its prior guidance of 8.2%–8.4%, driven by a favorable customer and product mix.
  • The company secured more than $60 billion in new orders during the quarter ended June 30, lifting its backlog to a record high.
  • Revenue is expected near the low end of its $11 billion to $12.5 billion guidance, below the analyst consensus of $11.67 billion.
  • SMCI shares jumped 17% in after-hours trading to roughly $30, while AI server rivals Dell and HPE also rallied.

Super Micro Computer stunned Wall Street on Tuesday with preliminary fiscal fourth-quarter results that showed a dramatic improvement in profitability, even as revenue came in below expectations. Shares of the San Jose-based AI server maker surged 17% to $29.92 in after-hours trading after the company said it expects gross margins nearly double what it had previously forecast.

The company now anticipates gross margins of 15% to 17% for the quarter ended June 30, sharply above its earlier guidance of 8.2% to 8.4%. Super Micro attributed the improvement to a "favorable customer and product mix," signalling that higher-margin AI infrastructure orders are displacing lower-margin commodity server sales.

A Record Backlog Signals Sustained AI Demand

Perhaps more striking than the margin surprise was the sheer volume of incoming business. Super Micro said it received more than $60 billion in new orders during the fiscal fourth quarter alone, pushing its backlog to record levels heading into fiscal year 2027.

> **"Dell Technologies gained more than 5% in extended trading, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise rallied 4.2%."**

The order surge reflects accelerating demand from tech giants and cloud providers racing to build out data-centre infrastructure for large language models and other AI applications. In June, Super Micro announced plans to raise $7 billion through equity and equity-linked financing to fulfill roughly $39 billion in orders for advanced AI servers from more than 20 customers.

"AI infrastructure firms have seen accelerated demand as tech companies and cloud providers ramp up investments in data centers to support large language models and other AI applications."

— Reuters, July 21, 2026

Revenue, however, is expected near the low end of the company's guidance range of $11 billion to $12.5 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected $11.67 billion, while FactSet pegged the consensus at $11.73 billion — suggesting some order fulfilment has been pushed into future quarters, consistent with the massive backlog buildup.

A Turbulent Year for SMCI

Tuesday's rally comes after a bruising stretch. The stock has fallen roughly 50% over the past year and was down 13% in 2026 before the after-hours move, battered by a string of controversies.

In March, the Department of Justice charged company co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw over an alleged scheme to smuggle U.S.-assembled servers to China. Liaw, who resigned from Super Micro in 2018, has pleaded not guilty. In June, two employees were detained in Taiwan as part of a separate investigation into alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. Super Micro has said it is not a target of that probe and is cooperating with authorities.

The company also narrowly avoided delisting from Nasdaq in early 2025 after failing to file financial reports on time, and a June announcement of $7 billion in equity financing sparked a sell-off on dilution fears.

Halo Effect Lifts AI Server Rivals

Super Micro's strong preliminary numbers rippled through the broader AI infrastructure sector. Dell Technologies gained more than 5% in extended trading, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise rallied 4.2%. Both had sold off earlier in July as investors rotated out of AI hardware names and into Big Tech software stocks — Dell fell 8% during the month, while Super Micro slipped 18%.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the thousands of Indian-origin professionals who power Silicon Valley's AI infrastructure ecosystem, Super Micro's record order pipeline signals that hiring and investment in data-centre buildouts will continue to accelerate. The company, headquartered in San Jose, counts Indian-origin executive Vik Malyala as its Chief Business Officer and employs more than 4,000 people globally. The broader AI infrastructure spending wave also has direct implications for Indian IT services firms like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, which provide consulting and integration services for large-scale data-centre deployments.

What's Next

Super Micro is scheduled to report full fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year results on August 11. Investors will watch for confirmation of the preliminary margin figures, details on the customer mix driving profitability, and guidance on how the record backlog will convert to revenue in fiscal 2027. With shares still roughly 50% below their 52-week highs, the key question is whether margin recovery and order momentum can be sustained — or whether legal overhangs and dilution concerns will keep weighing on the stock.
